input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds Customer (our party) with a post-term non-compete of 24 months, covering any competing product or service in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed it expressly bars acquisitions). That is walk-away territory under the rule: the post-term period exceeds 12 months and the scope is undefined/unlimited as to product and territory, so it fails the fallback on multiple material terms. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, which states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling or using any product or service or conducting business in any field or territory, and that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Deleting § 12.4 reaches the preferred position and removes the internal inconsistency; we have offered the narrowed fallback in the comment if Vendor needs protection for a specific product.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month, all-territory non-compete in § 12.4; it also contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have given no non-compete or exclusivity commitment. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a narrow restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month post-term non-compete binding Customer in § 12.4.
